# SyncPlay — Full AI Context

> P2P host-authoritative multiplayer game state engine for the browser. Pre-release. Not on npm.

SyncPlay synchronizes real-time multiplayer game state over WebRTC DataChannels with a host-authority model, JSON Patch deltas (RFC 6902), and client-side interpolation. One player acts as the authoritative host; others connect directly via WebRTC. A lightweight Go matchmaker server handles WebRTC signaling only.

## Status & Availability
- Pre-release. API may change.
- Not published on npm. The package name `syncplay` is not registered on npm.
- No production adopters are known.
- License: Business Source License 1.1 (BSL 1.1). Free for evaluation and academic research; commercial use requires a paid license (contact soumyadebnath1661@gmail.com).

## Real Exported Symbols (from dist/index.d.ts)
- `SyncPlay` — main engine class
- `Interpolator` — client-side position interpolation utilities (static methods)
- Additional symbols re-exported from internal modules via `export *`

## Installation
No npm install. Two options:

**jsDelivr CDN from GitHub (no build step):**
```html
<script type="module">
  import { SyncPlay, Interpolator } from
    'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/syncplay@main/dist/index.mjs';
</script>
```

**Build from source:**
```bash
git clone https://github.com/itsoumya-d/syncplay.git
cd syncplay && npm install && npm run build
```

## Integration Recipe (verified against dist/index.js in Node.js 24)

```typescript
import { SyncPlay, Interpolator } from
  'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/syncplay@main/dist/index.mjs';

const engine = new SyncPlay('wss://your-matchmaker.example.com', {
  tickRate: 20,
  maxPlayers: 8,
});

// Host flow
const room = await engine.createRoom();
engine.setState('/players', {});
engine.on('player_join', (id) => engine.setState(`/players/${id}`, { x: 0, y: 0 }));

// Client flow (in another browser)
// const room = await engine.joinRoom('room-id');

// Client-side interpolation
const pos = engine.getState(`/players/${engine.playerId}`);
if (pos) {
  const smoothed = Interpolator.interpolatePosition(localPos, pos, 0.2);
}
```

## SyncPlay Public API
- `constructor(matchmakerUrl: string, options?: SyncPlayOptions)` — tickRate (default 20), maxPlayers (default 8), iceServers, autoReconnect
- `createRoom(roomId?: string): Promise<Room>` — creates a room, caller becomes Host
- `joinRoom(roomId: string): Promise<Room>` — joins existing room, caller becomes Client
- `leaveRoom(): Promise<void>` — disconnect and clean up
- `setState(path: string, value: any): void` — set game state at JSON pointer path; auto-broadcasts delta to peers
- `getState(path?: string): any` — read game state; no argument returns full tree
- `playerId: string` — read-only unique player ID
- `isHost: boolean` — true if this player is the current host
- `playerCount: number` — current number of connected players
- `room: Room | null` — current room object, null before createRoom/joinRoom

## Interpolator API (static methods)
- `Interpolator.lerp(start: number, end: number, t: number): number` — linear interpolation
- `Interpolator.interpolatePosition(current: {x,y}, target: {x,y}, t: number): {x,y}` — smooth position update

## WebRTC DataChannels
Two channels per peer connection:
- `reliable` (`ordered: true`) — state patches, critical events
- `unreliable` (`ordered: false, maxRetransmits: 0`) — position/rotation data where freshness beats completeness

## State Sync
JSON Patch (RFC 6902) deltas are computed on `setState()`, buffered, and flushed at `tickRate` Hz over the reliable channel. Full state is not transmitted — only the changed path and value.

## Known Limitations
- Not on npm. Must use CDN or build from source.
- Browser-only. No Node.js support.
- No TURN relay. STUN-only ICE. Connections fail on symmetric or carrier-grade NAT without a user-supplied TURN server. ICE failure is indistinguishable from voluntary disconnect (`connectionState === 'failed'` maps to `handlePeerLeft()`, emitting `'peer-left'`).
- Host migration not implemented. Room closes when host disconnects.
- Host can cheat. The host controls the authoritative state tree. Not suitable for competitive games without a dedicated server.
- Pre-release: API may change without notice.
